findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as query parameter (?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX).
findings.actual: Query parameter api_key is rejected with HTTP 400 ('send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'). The API key must be sent via the X-API-Key header.
findings.how_found: Sent a GET request with ?api_key query parameter to /v1/listings and inspected the 400 error detail.
findings.impact: Any frontend or client adhering strictly to the documentation fails all authenticated requests immediately.

findings.documented: Returns token field with 24-hour expiration (expires_in: 86400) and user.name, with no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns access_token (not token) expiring in 900 seconds (15 minutes), refresh_token, refresh_url (/auth/refresh), and user without a name field.
findings.how_found: Inspected the JSON payload returned by POST /auth/login with valid demo credentials.
findings.impact: Clients expecting a 24-hour token silently break after 15 minutes unless an automated token refresh cycle using /auth/refresh is implemented.

findings.documented: Documentation states: 'Tokens are valid for 24 hours, so a single login is enough for one working session. There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts JSON {'refresh_token': '<token>'}, returning a refreshed access_token, refresh_token, and 900-second TTL.
findings.how_found: Observed refresh_url in the login response and verified successful token renewal via POST /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Crucial for long-lived user sessions; without using this endpoint, users get unexpectedly logged out after 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Takes page (1-indexed, default 1) and limit (default 20, max 200). Response format contains page and page_size.
findings.actual: The page parameter is ignored. Pagination strictly uses offset and limit. Maximum limit is capped at 50, not 200. Response payload contains limit, offset, count, total, and has_more instead of page/page_size.
findings.how_found: Tested varying page and limit values, observing identical first-page records when varying page, and limit clamping to 50 when requesting 200.
findings.impact: Paginating with page=2 fetches page 1 repeatedly, leading to infinite loops or incomplete data.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by your limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: The total field is underreported (reports 3,910 but 4,100 records are retrievable; rentals reports 1,478 vs 1,550 actual; projects reports 439 vs 460 actual). Stopping at total misses valid records.
findings.how_found: Paged past the reported total until has_more was false and results was empty, discovering 190 additional listings.
findings.impact: Data ingestion and analytics pipelines prematurely terminate, omitting approximately 5% of available records.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing object.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{id} returns HTTP 404 Not Found. The correct endpoint is pluralized: GET /v1/listings/{id}.
findings.how_found: Attempted fetching individual listings via both singular and plural paths; singular returned 404 while plural returned 200.
findings.impact: Listing detail views break with 404 errors when using the documented singular path.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: Returns HTTP 404 Not Found for all valid listing IDs; the endpoint was never implemented or deployed.
findings.how_found: Requested /similar for multiple verified active listing IDs and received 404 responses across all tests.
findings.impact: Similar listing carousels fail unless synthesized client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates (median price, price per sqft, locality breakdown) for your city.
findings.how_found: Called /v1/analytics/summary with valid auth headers; received 404.
findings.impact: Dashboard summary statistics cannot be retrieved from the server and must be computed from raw records.

findings.actual: All /v1/favourites endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found. The working endpoint is /v1/saved, which takes {'listing_id': '...'} on POST.
findings.how_found: Tested /v1/favourites and received 404; discovered /v1/saved returning 200 OK and supporting full saved listings CRUD.
findings.impact: Favorites functionality fails entirely if using the documented endpoint name and request body structure.

findings.documented: Not mentioned in documentation (which instead describes /v1/favourites).
findings.actual: Implements GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved (with body {'listing_id': '...'}), and DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id}, returning HTTP 201 on creation.
findings.how_found: Probed common REST resource naming conventions after /v1/favourites failed.
findings.impact: Essential for fulfilling the saved listings requirement of the application.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Inactive listings are not excluded server side; 867 listing records have is_live: false.
findings.how_found: Filtered full collection for is_live == False and confirmed the API serves them by default.
findings.impact: Without client-side is_live filtering, users are shown stale or withdrawn properties.

findings.documented: Supports query parameters min_price, max_price, furnishing, and project_id.
findings.actual: min_price, max_price, and project_id are completely ignored by the server. The furnishing filter returns mixed results including other furnishing types.
findings.how_found: Sent requests with min_price=10M and max_price=12M and received records priced at 6.6M; tested project_id filter and received arbitrary project IDs.
findings.impact: Users relying on server filtering receive completely incorrect search results unless the client applies filtering locally.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: 336 listings from the magichomes portal report carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square meters (values < 250 for 2-4 BHK apartments) rather than square feet.
findings.how_found: Analyzed carpet_area distribution by website; magichomes had a distinct cluster between 34 and 240, while all other portals were >= 276 sqft.
findings.impact: Displaying raw values misleads buyers by showing 80 sqft for a 2 BHK; computing price/sqft naively produces rates ~10.76x too high.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees (e.g. 8900000, 21400000).
findings.actual: Project prices are not in integer Rupees. Values < 10 represent Crores (e.g. 3.78 = 3.78 Cr) and values >= 10 represent Lakhs (e.g. 66.1 = 66.1 L).
findings.how_found: Cross-referenced project prices with listing prices in the same projects and observed that project min/max were formatted as raw decimal amounts without unit multipliers.
findings.impact: A project with price_max 3.78 would be interpreted as 3.78 rupees instead of 37,800,000 INR; sorting by price_max puts 99.8 L above 3.78 Cr.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 36 listing records describe physical impossibilities: 9 with negative prices, 9 with floor > total_floors, 9 with carpet_area > super_built_up_area, and 9 with swapped lat/lon placed in the Arctic Ocean.
findings.how_found: Audited field constraints against physical reality across all 4,100 listings.
findings.impact: Corrupt listings degrade search quality and corrupt financial aggregations unless sanitized.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings. Every listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 9 listing records are fake bait listings posted with monthly rental rates (6,470 to 16,320 INR) instead of sale prices to generate enquiries.
findings.how_found: Identified extreme low price/sqft outliers (< 20 INR/sqft) corresponding precisely to monthly rental figures for apartments in those localities.
findings.impact: Bait listings deceive prospective buyers and distort market averages unless identified and filtered.

findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with Z suffix reflecting when listings were posted.
findings.actual: 9 listings have future posted_at timestamps occurring in 2026 and 2027 (e.g. 2027-07-03), which is impossible for historical postings before the reference date.
findings.how_found: Evaluated posted_at dates against the reference moment 2026-09-10T00:00:00+05:30.
findings.impact: Recent-listing filters and recency sorting surface future records at the top.

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in the project. It is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: total_listings disagrees with actual active listings in listings.json for 119 projects (and GET /v1/listings?project_id=... does not filter by project_id).
findings.how_found: Aggregated listings by project_id and compared counts against reported project total_listings.
findings.impact: Projects display stale or inaccurate available unit counts.
